nodes.title: Choose the next point
nodes.transcript: For f(x) = x², the gradient is 2x. Starting at x = 2 gives gradient 4. A gradient descent step subtracts the learning rate times the gradient: x_next = x − α × 2x.
nodes.prompt: Start at x = 2 with learning rate α = 0.25. Where does one gradient descent step land?

nodes.title: Check the direction
nodes.transcript: Adding 0.25 × 4 would move from x = 2 to x = 3, where the loss rises from 4 to 9. Gradient descent subtracts the positive gradient. Return to the question and try the downhill direction.

nodes.title: A step downhill
nodes.transcript: The next point is 2 − 0.25 × 4 = 1. The loss decreases from f(2) = 4 to f(1) = 1. This illustrates one step on this particular function, not a convergence guarantee for arbitrary learning rates.
